## GPU execution (`CUDA`, `DEVICE`) {#sec-ch14-gpu}

### Summary

A block's tensors are created on the CPU by its constructor. The driver moves the block (`block->to(device)`) or the
whole mesh (`mesh->to(device)`) before initialising. The device is `cuda:<DEVICE_ID>`, or `cuda:<LOCAL_RANK>` when
`DEVICE_ID` is negative (@sec-ch14-launch). Torch operators run on the device. snapy's own kernels (reconstruction,
equation of state, boundaries and others) have a CPU and a CUDA implementation behind a dispatch stub
(@sec-ch01-dispatch). Collectives and decisions run on the host (@sec-ch14-collectives), so they read device values back.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Runs the same code on a CUDA device: blocks are moved with `to(device)` and kernels dispatch to CUDA.

**Data.** Every tensor of a block, moved once before initialisation; host read-backs for collectives.

**Placement.** The driver, before `initialize`; snapy's kernels through their dispatch stubs every stage.

**Activation.** CMake `CUDA=ON` and environment `DEVICE=cuda` (`DEVICE_ID`). Default: CPU.

**Guarantee / limits.** Same scheme; CPU and CUDA round-off differ, by an amount the code does not bound.

**Evidence.** The Tests layer below, @tbl-ch14-gpu-tests.
:::

Local symbols: none. This section uses no mathematical symbol beyond the cell counts of its tests.

### Derivation

There is no equation. Why a run can end up on the CPU without saying so, and why a CPU build skips the CUDA tests,
in four steps:

1. *The driver asks two questions.* `run_hydro` moves the block to `cuda:<id>` only if `torch::cuda::is_available()`
   and the layout's device is `cuda`; it prints "Running on CUDA" only then ({{< code examples/run_hydro.cpp main >}}).
2. *There is no else.* Otherwise the device stays `torch::kCPU`, with no message.
3. *The test gate asks the build first.* `snapy_cuda_test_enabled` returns `torch::cuda::is_available()` only when
   snapy was compiled with `USE_CUDA`, and false otherwise.
4. *Hence* a CPU build never enters a CUDA test, even with a GPU visible, and a `DEVICE=cuda` run on a machine without
   CUDA runs on the CPU.

Round-off: CPU and CUDA kernels sum stencil terms and reductions in different orders, so their results differ by
round-off. The size depends on each kernel's summation order on each device, which the code does not fix, so no
bound is derived here; the tests below assert measured tolerances instead.

### Numerical method

The example driver `run_hydro` picks the device only if `torch::cuda::is_available()` and `DEVICE=cuda`. Otherwise it
stays on the CPU and prints nothing; "Running on CUDA" is printed only when the device is used
(`torch::cuda::is_available`, {{< code examples/run_hydro.cpp main >}}).

The reconstruction kernels launch one CUDA block per line. A line longer than 1024 cells does not fit in one CUDA
block, so `recon_tile_width` returns a tile width instead. It starts at 256 and halves until the tile, its
stencil halo and the weights fit in 48 KiB of shared memory; the caller then runs the tiled kernel
(`recon_tile_width`, {{< code src/recon/recon_dispatch.cu recon_tile_width >}}).

A CUDA test of snapy runs only when snapy was built with CUDA *and* torch sees a device.
`snapy_cuda_test_enabled` returns false in a CPU build even when a GPU is visible
({{< code tests/cuda_test_gate.hpp snapy_cuda_test_enabled >}}).

Each host read-back (`.item()`) of a device value synchronises the device. Per step, they come from the time-step
MIN, the redo flags, the signal check, the cycle-line meters, the gravity-work fixer and, with the implicit solver,
one finiteness screen per stage. Within a stage and in the redo check, the CUDA vapour repair adds its failures to a
device count that the redo flags carry (@sec-ch14-collectives) instead of reading them back. Their count per step at
the pin was not measured for this chapter.[^ch14-gpu-sync]

[^ch14-gpu-sync]: An open upstream issue (chengcli/snapy#291) counted 33 per step on a small 2-D moist grid with
    snapy 2.11.2, against 7 on 2.10.9. The pin includes later changes that remove host syncs, so that count is not
    the pin's.

### Code

**A minimal input.** A CUDA build and the environment, with the card unchanged:

```bash
cmake -B build -DCUDA=ON && cmake --build build
cd build/bin && DEVICE=cuda DEVICE_ID=0 ./run_hydro.release -i jupiter_evap_precip_1d.yaml
```

This needs a machine with an NVIDIA GPU and the CUDA toolkit. `run_hydro.release` needs a deck with a `reactions:`
card, as in [Install and run](#sec-preface-install).

**What is refused, and why.** Nothing at the device choice: a missing GPU falls back to the CPU (steps 1 and 2). A
multi-process CUDA run over Gloo or an external group is refused at its first message, "Gloo communication requires
CPU tensors" (@sec-ch14-backends).

**The excerpt.** Steps 1 and 2, in `run_hydro`:

```cpp
torch::Device device(torch::kCPU);
if (torch::cuda::is_available() && op_block->layout()->device() == "cuda") {
  std::cout << "Running on CUDA" << std::endl;
  ...
  device = torch::Device(torch::kCUDA, device_id);
}
block->to(device);
```

|---|---|---|---|
| `test_weno5_cuda_line` (CUDA builds) | reconstruction on CUDA matches the CPU for lines of 32, 1024, 1025, 1030 and 1280 cells | $10^{-12}$ | round-off of the stencil sums |
| `test_cubed_sphere_exchange` `subdivided_panel_exchange_matches_one_block_cuda` | on CUDA, $n_{b2} = 2, 4$ give the faces, $\Delta x_2$ and the density after one stage of $n_{b2} = 1$ | bitwise (`torch::equal`) | @sec-ch14-repro |
| `test_x1_seam_split_*_cuda` (CUDA builds) | the $x_1$ seam arms on CUDA | as the CPU arms | @sec-ch03-x1seams |
| `*_cuda_python` (CUDA builds) | nine Python tests rerun with `--device cuda`: vapour-fix failure, vapour-fix stale count, saturation redo, two flux-positivity cases, fourth-order well-balanced, $x_1$ centroid, radial-exact work, scalar flux covariance (`test_scalar_flux_covariance_cuda`) | as the CPU runs | same scripts and assertions |
| `test_vic_moist_device_python` (CUDA builds) | one implicit moist step on CPU and on CUDA agree | $10^{-9}$ max abs. | about 17 times the $5.8\times10^{-11}$ of the source comment (H100; no sha or deck given, so not evidence here) |
| `test_shallow_splash_ucx_cuda_decomp` (`FULL_TESTS`) | shallow-water splash decompositions on two GPUs over UCX; exits 125 without them | the runner's | `run_shallow_splash_decomp.py` |

device.[^ch14-gpu-run]

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
- The per-step cost of the host read-backs on GPU was not measured at the pin; an upstream issue reports a launch-bound
  grid slowing down with their count.[^ch14-gpu-cost]
- A driver that asks for CUDA on a machine without it runs on the CPU silently (`run_hydro`).
:::

[^ch14-gpu-cost]: chengcli/snapy#291 (open): on a 178 by 120 moist grid on one A100, a step cost 42.1 ms on 2.11.2
    against 27.4 ms on 2.10.9, with 3005 against 2061 kernels and 33 against 7 `.item()` calls per step. The
    numbers are the issue's and were not re-measured here.
